newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly up despite cash break.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly up despite cash break.

text.p: CME lumber futures showed mixed technical and short covering support much of the day and closed mostly higher despite sliding cash lumber prices, traders said.
Futures started to look oversold and showed strength Thursday after holding a trend line around $372, basis January, they said.
"Just as always, you overdo it on the way up and overdo it on the way down and I think futures have come to the first stopping point," said Curt Cunningham, President Pacific Futures Trading.
Lumber futures closed mostly off $2.50 per thousand board feet to up $5.70 with January off $2.50 at #78.00 and March up $2.80 at $374.00 per tbf.

Expectations cash prices will bottom soon and start a seasonal rise during the lighter end of the year production period also lent support. However, cash prices continued to correct from the sharp jump earlier this month, they added.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce Friday at $398 per tbf, down $27 from midweek and down $75 from last Friday. They said dealers refused to pay higher asking levels reached during the frenzy over Canada's individual company export quotas.
The Framing Lumber Composite Price registered its largest one-week drop since 1993, giving up $33 of the $45 it had gained the previous two weeks, Random Lengths added.
